title: Regiment and Lantern
premise: In the winter of the great storms, Rosalind Zhou keeps the lantern at Gullwatch Point, the last keeper on a coast being emptied by evacuation orders. When the bridge closes for the season, Rosalind, their ailing mother, and their estranged brother Edmund are trapped with one berth left on the final relief boat. As the storms strip away pretense, old wounds over an inherited deed — and the truth of who actually kept the family alive all these years — surface with the tide. In the end, Rosalind gives up the berth, sends Edmund and their mother across, and stays to keep the light burning alone, discovering that inheritance is not what is given to you but what you refuse to abandon.
about_author: A. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs from decommissioned stations along the northern coast. Their fiction draws on the marginalia keepers left in official records — weather notes, griefs, and small rebellions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Opening in the routine of the light: polishing lenses, logging weather, measuring life in portable things. The first evacuation notice arrives by supply boat, casually worded. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competence; Rosalind begins mentally inventorying what can be carried and what cannot.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The bridge authority announces seasonal closure; the last guaranteed crossing is weeks away, and berths are limited to two per household. Rosalind's mother, Mei, insists she will stay with the house. Emotional beat: the first open fracture — three people, one berth, and no one willing to say it aloud.

chapters.title: What Edmund Carried Back
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The brother returns after eleven years away, ostensibly to help but really to claim his share of the deed before the coast is condemned. He finds the house maintained, the ledgers meticulous, all in Rosalind's hand. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Deed
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A storm forces the siblings into the cellar, where they find their father's original deed — naming Edmund sole heir — alongside Rosalind's decades of unpaid labor recorded in the margins. Emotional beat: memory as evidence; the past stops being negotiable.

chapters.title: Half-Light
chapters.summary: Mei's POV. Flashback chapters braided through present: how Mei signed the deed under pressure, how she watched Rosalind absorb the injustice without complaint. In the present, she quietly asks Rosalind to take the berth. Emotional beat: a mother's reckoning with her own complicity.

chapters.title: The Relief Boat That Turned Back
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The promised early boat fails to arrive — seas too rough, schedule cut. Radio contact frays. Edmund, panicking, considers the mainland connections he abandoned. Emotional beat: rising desperation; the outside world reveals its indifference.

chapters.title: Salt in the Seams
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Storm damage floods the lower rooms; Edmund works beside Rosalind through the night saving the logbooks and the lens. For the first time he sees the station as Rosalind sees it — not property but vocation. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness between rivals.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Word comes: one berth remains on the final boat, non-negotiable. Each secretly tries to give it to another — Mei to Rosalind, Rosalind to Mei, Edmund, hollowed out, offers it back to both. Emotional beat: love expressed as refusal; the climax of the moral argument.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Climax. Rosalind's POV. At dawn, Rosalind puts Mei aboard by force of will and forgives Edmund at the rail — not for the deed, but for coming back. The boat vanishes into the squall. Rosalind climbs the tower alone as the greatest storm of the year makes landfall. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into choice.

chapters.title: Regiment and Lantern
chapters.summary: Resolution. Rosalind's POV, months later. Spring survey boat finds the light still burning, logs immaculate, a letter from Mei enclosed in the record. Officials offer reassignment inland; Rosalind requests the station itself, now theirs by condemnation buyout — the only heir who stayed. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as devotion; the lamp lit against an empty sea.
